He added that his time playing alongside DeChambeau gave him a clear understanding of what the power-hitter could have accomplished on the PGA Tour. This admission suggests that the gap between the tours was not as wide as some critics claimed. Koepka believes that if the LIV players had remained, the competition would have been fierce. “We all have a good feel how we would have fared on any tour,” he noted. He believes Scheffler “would have won a lot of his golf tournaments,” but he insists that the LIV contingent “would have put up a good fight.” The Impact of the 2022 Exodus The departure of major champions created a vacuum that Scheffler filled with historic consistency. Critics often point to the fact that three of Scheffler’s four major wins occurred after the mass exodus of top talent. Koepka’s comments provide a counter-narrative to the debate about the strength of his resume. He suggests that the presence of players like DeChambeau and himself would not have stopped Scheffler from winning, but it would have made the path much harder. The five-time major winner implies that the competition level on the PGA Tour would have remained elite had the split not occurred. DeChambeau, who won the 2024 U.S. Open, is a central figure in this discussion. According to GolfMagic , DeChambeau’s 2024 victory over Rory McIlroy by a single shot proves his game remains at the highest level. The two-time major winner now faces a new challenge as he plans his 2027 schedule on the DP World Tour. Unless the circuit alters its stance, DeChambeau faces a PGA Tour ban for at least 12 months following the LIV Golf collapse. New PGA Tour commissioner Brian Rolapp has expressed sentiments that make a return for DeChambeau in 2027 seem unlikely. This regulatory hurdle forces the American to look elsewhere for competitive play. DeChambeau’s New Path and Future Projects DeChambeau is not sitting idle while waiting for a potential PGA Tour return. He has committed to an exemption on the DP World Tour, leveraging his U.S. Open status to pick and choose his schedule. GolfMagic reports that he will target lucrative Rolex Series events and tournaments surrounding the four men’s majors. His journey begins in South Africa with the Nedbank Golf Challenge at Sun City, scheduled for 3-6 December. He is expected to follow this with the Dubai Desert Classic over 21-24 January. These events will serve as a tune-up for the major stretch in 2027. Beyond tournament play, DeChambeau is expanding his footprint in the golf community through development projects. The Sun reported that the golfer announced a new initiative to design a championship course in his hometown of Clovis, California. Titled ‘The Orchard,’ the 18-hole facility will feature an on-site farmer’s market and various community amenities. A signed statement from DeChambeau read, “There is a deep responsibility to give back to the region that provided us with so much.” He intends for this course to serve as the initial one among many fully procured DeChambeau Designs. The Sun observed that the project seeks to transform the local area, in a signed statement from DeChambeau wrote, “It’s time to make a better future for our next generation.” DeChambeau anticipates approval for the project within 18 months, with amenities like a driving range coming sooner. He expressed a broader hope for the facility, stating, “It is our hope that this will be a place where everyone in the world can come and enjoy the fruits of our labor here in the Central Valley.” This community focus contrasts with the high-stakes professional golf world where Koepka and Scheffler compete. The golfer also maintains a strong digital presence, with his YouTube channel boasting over 3 million subscribers and multiple long-form videos posted monthly. The Sun noted that DeChambeau was one of LIV’s poster boys before Saudi funding pulled out, sending the league into a deathspin. Despite the league’s collapse, DeChambeau remains a dominant force, preparing for his next chapter on the DP World Tour starting in December.

item.title: Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal
item.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a new two-and-a-half-year deal [Getty Images] Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract at the Championship club until 2029. The 33-year-old German's existing deal was expiring at the end of this season after being handed the role permanently last December. Eckert's future was thrown into doubt over the summer, having been at the centre of an investigation by the Football Association over his role in the 'Spygate' scandal. He could have been handed a lengthy suspension that would have threatened his job, but was ultimately given a suspended six-week ban and £28,000 fine. "I'm very happy we have come to the point that we can make it official now," Eckert told the club website. More to follow. Latest Southampton news and analysis

item.title: Dana White reveals condition for his team to receive time off to GTA 6
item.description: Dana White reveals condition for his team to receive time off to GTA 6 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . GTA 6 is now officially out, and the entire world is going crazy to play it . While many people have booked their holidays to play the game, some companies have willingly given leave to their employees. Described as one of the biggest video games in the industry , GTA 6 has generated worldwide hype that is crazy to match. With UFC’s Conor McGregor allowing his 400 employees to take time off to play, and Sean Strickland cautioning youngsters not to play, Dana White has different responsibilities for his employees. In a recent video uploaded on UFC’s and PowerSlap’s Instagram page, boss Dana White was asked what his social media team needed to do in order for him to give them a day off to play GTA 6. In the latest version of the game, social media plays a big role, and White particularly used that angle to approach his team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When asked the question of how many likes they need to hit for the day off, White laughed and bluntly responded, “300,000.” However, as of now, that goal seems far from being attainable. As of this writing, the post has received roughly 68K likes. Joining in on the fun, UFC Europe and Zuffa Boxing also left behind two hilarious comments. White himself is currently working through a very rigorous schedule. Power Slap 27 took place on Nov. 19, 2026, in Doha, Qatar, before UFC Fight Night is also scheduled to take place in the same location on Nov. 21, 2026. Later, UFC 335 will return on Dec. 12, 2026, in Las Vegas, before another Fight Night card in Dallas, Texas, on Jan. 16, 2026. item.title: Grading the Browns defense: New faces, similar results at the bye week
item.description: Going into the 2026 season, the Cleveland Browns defense was undergoing some changes that were seen as major from the outside. Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was traded to the Los Angeles Rams , and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz chose to leave the team after being passed up for the head coaching job. In the Myles Garrett trade, the team received defensive end Jared Verse from the Rams (who won defensive rookie of the year in 2024 and is a two-time Pro Bowler), who isn’t necessarily the same caliber player as Garrett but has shown signs of being a really good edge rusher while in LA. The Browns hired Atlanta Falcons passing game coordinator Mike Rutenberg to be their defensive coordinator. Analysts and fans were concerned about the defense taking a step back after losing Garrett and Schwartz, but it appears that the defense is doing just fine. Just like we did with the offense earlier this week , it is time to size up the Browns defense at the bye week and give it a grade. What has changed? Outside of losing Garrett and Schwartz, not much. After losing linebacker Devin Bush in free agency, the team replaced him with linebacker Quincy Williams. Cornerback Martin Emerson also left, but outside of those minor subtractions, the team has essentially returned most of their group from last season. Defensive tackle Mason Graham has emerged as the best player on the defensive line. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger might be a top 10 linebacker in this league, maybe even Top 5. Extending cornerback Denzel Ward and safety Grant Delpit were no-brainers. Ward, who is playing at a top-5 level, will likely be an All-Pro this season, and Delpit has been one of the more underrated safeties in the league. After being acquired in a trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, cornerback Tyson Campbell has fit in well in his second full year with the team. When Schwartz wasn’t retained as the defensive coordinator, many wondered how the scheme would look. Rutenberg, also known as Rudy, decided to not change the scheme but instead tweak it. Schwartz’s defenses weren’t complex in terms of how the scheme looked. Not much creativity in terms of mixing up the coverages and disguising looks. Schwartz also failed to make the necessary adjustments, and his defenses were easy to decipher against better offensive minds. Rutenberg has made tweaks to the scheme but is still keeping the core principles that made the Browns defense elite last season. item.content:encoded: Going into the 2026 season, the Cleveland Browns defense was undergoing some changes that were seen as major from the outside. Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was traded to the Los Angeles Rams , and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz chose to leave the team after being passed up for the head coaching job. In the Myles Garrett trade, the team received defensive end Jared Verse from the Rams (who won defensive rookie of the year in 2024 and is a two-time Pro Bowler), who isn’t necessarily the same caliber player as Garrett but has shown signs of being a really good edge rusher while in LA. The Browns hired Atlanta Falcons passing game coordinator Mike Rutenberg to be their defensive coordinator. Analysts and fans were concerned about the defense taking a step back after losing Garrett and Schwartz, but it appears that the defense is doing just fine. Just like we did with the offense earlier this week , it is time to size up the Browns defense at the bye week and give it a grade. What has changed? Outside of losing Garrett and Schwartz, not much. After losing linebacker Devin Bush in free agency, the team replaced him with linebacker Quincy Williams. Cornerback Martin Emerson also left, but outside of those minor subtractions, the team has essentially returned most of their group from last season. Defensive tackle Mason Graham has emerged as the best player on the defensive line. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger might be a top 10 linebacker in this league, maybe even Top 5. Extending cornerback Denzel Ward and safety Grant Delpit were no-brainers. Ward, who is playing at a top-5 level, will likely be an All-Pro this season, and Delpit has been one of the more underrated safeties in the league. After being acquired in a trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, cornerback Tyson Campbell has fit in well in his second full year with the team. When Schwartz wasn’t retained as the defensive coordinator, many wondered how the scheme would look. Rutenberg, also known as Rudy, decided to not change the scheme but instead tweak it. Schwartz’s defenses weren’t complex in terms of how the scheme looked. Not much creativity in terms of mixing up the coverages and disguising looks. Schwartz also failed to make the necessary adjustments, and his defenses were easy to decipher against better offensive minds. Rutenberg has made tweaks to the scheme but is still keeping the core principles that made the Browns defense elite last season. Browns defense pre-bye (last season) 5th in EPA/per play 3rd in Defensive Success Rate 15th in Defensive Dropback EPA/per play 14th in Defensive Dropback Success Rate 2nd in Defensive Rush EPA/per play 1st in Defensive Rush Success Rate Browns defense pre-bye (2026 season) 10th in EPA/per play 8th in Defensive Success Rate 9th in Defensive Dropback EPA/per play 4th in Defensive Dropback success rate 26th in Defensive Rush EPA/per play 17th in Defensive Rush Success rate Overall, going from a top 5 defense to a top 10 is not that bad. One of the more surprising stats is how the team is still top 10 in pressures despite losing Garrett. It speaks volumes as to how talented their defensive line is. Players such as defensive end Isaiah McGuire and tackles Adin Huntington and Maliek Collins have contributed to the pressure. For all the talk about how versatile the Browns' defense has become under DC Mike Rutenberg, they still look downright special when they just lock up man-to-man and dare teams to beat them. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 15, 2026 In terms of the play on the back end, the Browns play man coverage more than anyone in the league, and they are really good at it. Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to stand out, and it’s not long before he becomes a full-time starter because of how well he’s played. Defensive coverages weeks 1-10 via @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/kHyr8wIvIn — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) November 17, 2026 Slot corner was considered a weakness going into the season, but cornerback Myles Harden might have fixed it. Harden has shown his effectiveness on blitz packages, but his coverage is what stands out. Harden had a rough training camp, but he was able to bounce back and show his contributions at a high level. Teams will regularly throw in his direction, but that is a testament to Ward and Campbell more than anything else. What Needs to Improve? The run defense . It’s not a major concern, but the run defense has taken a step back from last season. As good as the Browns defensive line is, they lack someone big along the interior. Cleveland’s defensive line is small but quick in terms of their get-off, but against teams that run trap/wham run concepts, they are susceptible to giving up chunk yards. The tackling also needs to improve, but some of the tackling woes can be due to the team’s attacking style they play. In terms of who needs to improve from a player standpoint, it’s Jared Verse. Verse hasn’t had the season he’s wanted, but he has to find a way to convert pressures into sacks. Last Sunday against the Texans, Verse played one of his best games as a Brown, but it can only get better if he builds off that performance. Browns DE Jared Verse registered season-high marks in pressures (5) and pressure rate (17.9%) against the Texans. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 16, 2026 It's no secret Jared Verse has had a disappointing season, but Sunday was arguably his best game of the season and as impressive as Tyson Campbell's interception was on this play, Verse made it happen. Gets around Aireontae Ersery and pressures Stroud into a rushed throw. If he… pic.twitter.com/7r91tBqlIK — 𝚂𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎𝚛 𝙶𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚊𝚗 (@Spencito_) November 18, 2026 Grade Despite losing Garrett, the Browns defense is still a top 10 unit in the league. Rutenberg has been an upgrade over Schwartz. The team is still missing that alpha in the defensive end room, but overall, for a unit that many people thought would fall off, the fact that this unit has been top-10 has been a surprise, but not to those who pay close attention. item.title: Man City vs Fulham: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction
item.description: Man City vs Fulham: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction Man City vs Fulham Preview: Pressure Builds on Enzo Maresca as Cottagers Eye Etihad Upset Manchester City have gone from setting the pace to chasing it. Seven straight Premier League wins opened the campaign, then reality hit. Three consecutive defeats have dragged Enzo Maresca’s side down to third, six points behind Arsenal. Form changes quickly in this league, but the numbers now matter and City’s trend is ugly. Normally, Fulham would be the ideal opponent to stop the slide. City have beaten the Cottagers in their last 17 top-flight meetings. Stretch that across all competitions and it becomes 20 in a row. That is not a rivalry, it is a pattern. The problem for City is that patterns only last until they don’t. Fulham arrive in better shape than many will expect. Alvaro Arbeloa’s side have taken eight points from their last four league matches, built on two wins and two draws. While City have taken nothing from their last three, Fulham have been organised, stubborn and increasingly awkward to play against. Those are useful traits when heading to the Etihad. Photo IMAGO Man City form raises real questions The losses to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest were not a blip because there have now been three of them, and all exposed something. City were beaten 2-1 by Villa, edged out 1-0 by Brighton and then conceded three in a 3-1 defeat at Forest. That sequence tells its own story. They are not controlling matches well enough and they are giving opponents too many openings. Selection issues in defence only add to the concern. Marc Guehi is a major doubt after asking to come off at half-time against Nottingham Forest and then withdrawing from England duty. Abdukodir Khusanov also needs assessing after leaving Uzbekistan’s squad. If neither makes it, Josko Gvardiol may have to move inside from left-back, with Nico O’Reilly potentially returning to the side. Antoine Semenyo remains unavailable with a knee injury and is not expected back until December. None of this amounts to a crisis on its own, but when a team is already losing games, defensive uncertainty tends to get magnified. Fulham form offers genuine encouragement Fulham’s case is straightforward. They are compact, harder to break down and carrying enough belief to think they can frustrate City for long periods. Josh King went off late in the 1-1 draw with Newcastle, though Arbeloa said it looked like “nothing serious”, and the player himself stated he was “all good fitness-wise”. That points towards availability. Tom Cairney is less certain after his knee issue, while Joachim Andersen appears likely to be involved despite picking up a foot injury on international duty and then completing 90 minutes in Denmark’s next match. Up front, Rodrigo Muniz has given Arbeloa a decision to make after scoring from the bench against Newcastle, with Gonzalo Garcia under pressure for his starting place. More importantly, Fulham’s recent away work deserves attention. They drew 0-0 at Liverpool and fully earned it. They also took a 1-1 result at Villa Park. Those are not smash-and-grab outcomes, they are signs of a side that knows how to stay in games away from home. Man City vs Fulham prediction This comes down to trust. Right now, City have not earned much of it. Fulham have. That does not mean Fulham are suddenly favourites, because City still have the better squad and the stronger attacking ceiling. It does mean the game should be viewed through form, not through old results. If City start sharply, the crowd settles and the narrative changes. If Fulham keep it tight for an hour, anxiety will creep in. That is where this becomes interesting. The sensible call is a low-scoring match and a very live chance of dropped points for the home side. Fulham have shown at difficult grounds that they can stay compact and disciplined, and City have shown over the last three games that they can be rattled. Prediction, Man City 1-1 Fulham.

item.title: German broadcaster Sky won't send any staff to F1 Qatar GP
item.description: ILLUSTRATION - The logo of the television channel Sky is displayed in front of the headquarters of Sky Deutschland Fernsehen GmbH & Co. KG. (is associated with: «German broadcaster Sky won't send any staff to F1 Qatar GP») Matthias Balk/dpa Sky TV won't be sending any staff to the Formula One Qatar Grand Prix due to security reasons in connection with the war in Iran, the German broadcaster said on Friday. The entire race weekend will be broadcast live as usual, but Sky won't have an on-site editorial team for the event on November 27-29. Qatar is one of the mediators in the deadlocked conflict between the United States and Iran, and has been among the targets of missile attacks from Iran. Despite the tension in the Middle East, F1 plans to conclude the season as scheduled in Qatar and in Abu Dhabi on December 6. Sky still intends to send a team to report live from Abu Dhabi. However, it continues to "monitor developments and assess the situation on an ongoing basis."

item.title: Vinicius Jr back after ban for Madrid but not guaranteed starting spot
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior warms up prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League Quarterfinal Second Leg soccer match between Bayern Munich and Real Madrid at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Vinicius Jr back after ban for Madrid but not guaranteed starting spot») Sven Hoppe/dpa José Mourinho said Real Madrid “love and need” Vinícius Júnior but has offered the Brazil forward no guarantees he will be back in the starting line-up for Saturday’s clash against Celta Vigo after completing a four-match ban. Vinícius Jr has faced much criticism in Spain this season, having scored one goal in 12 appearances for Madrid prior to his red card for a hair pull against Villarreal in October. It did not help his case that Madrid won all four of their matches for which he was suspended, including last month’s El Clásico victory away to Barcelona. But Madrid were given a reminder of what the 26-year-old is capable of as Vinícius Jr scored five goals in two appearances for Brazil over the international break, leading to inevitable questions as Mourinho faced the media on Friday. “Starting, on the bench, in the stands, it makes no difference,” Mourinho said. “It’s strange because a couple of weeks ago people were talking about him as if he had a huge problem and now, after scoring those goals, we can’t stop talking about him, whether he plays or not. “I think it’s too much. He’s incredible. We love him and we need him. There are no privileged players here, no one who has to play by default. Everyone works for the team. And then there’s this narrative that he has to leave because he isn’t playing enough. “Real Madrid need a strong squad, one that means the coach doesn’t have to worry about injuries.” Vinícius Jr spoke about his issues at Madrid during the international break, saying he had been affected by Brazil’s early exit from the World Cup and speculation over a potential move away from the Bernabeu. “He’s a young man who has reflected on himself,” Mourinho said. “Maybe he could have kept those comments to him, but I never like criticizing someone for being open. “Winter is now beginning, the real grind…That’s where Vinicius can make a huge difference. He can be decisive. He’s a player the whole dressing room loves. “Sometimes there are players the dressing room isn’t fond of, players it doesn’t really embrace as one of its own. Vinicius is the opposite.” Madrid start the weekend three points behind leaders and rivals Barcelona and can move level as they play first, but Mourinho said a Celta Vigo side down in 11th place should not be overlooked. “Celta are much better than their points total suggests,” he said. “They already beat us last season, they’re playing in Europe, and perhaps that’s costing them some points, but tomorrow that factor won’t exist.” Former Manchester United boss Mourinho dismissed a question about 16-year-old forward JJ Gabriel, who has left Old Trafford and is now expected to join Madrid. item.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
item.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal. Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season. An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations. Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences. And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot. The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029. Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now. "There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come." More follows

item.title: Two Spurs stars return to training ahead of Ipswich clash
item.description: Two Spurs stars return to training ahead of Ipswich clash Savio and Lucas Bergvall were both back in Tottenham training ahead of their match against Ipswich this weekend. The pair have both been ruled out with injury since the 1-1 draw against Manchester United last month . Savio with a muscular injury, and Bergvall with a knee injury. After Mathys Tel went off injured against Leeds after a strong tackle from Jayden Bogle, Savio’s reintroduction into the Spurs setup will be a massive boost for Roberto De Zerbi. The Italian hinted that the Brazilian could return after the international break before their draw against Leeds, saying, “Mudryk and Savio after the international break.” Mykhailo Mudryk, who has been sidelined since his debut against Nottingham Forest in September, and Tel were both not pictured in training. Asked after the Leeds clash about Tel’s injury, De Zerbi said, “Bad injury. Now we have to make the medical checks and in the next day we will know the problem.”

item.title: Max Verstappen: “I really thought that we would not win a race this year”
item.description: Motorsport photo Heading into the Las Vegas Grand Prix on a run of eight consecutive podiums, Max Verstappen looks every bit the force who dominated Formula 1 earlier this decade. Back in March, however, the four-time world champion was braced for his first winless campaign since 2015. Speaking during Las Vegas media day, Verstappen reflected on the scale of Red Bull Racing ’s mid-season recovery during Formula 1’s sweeping 2026 chassis and engine overhaul - the team’s first year running its in-house Red Bull Ford power unit. "Did I personally expect it to be like this after the first few rounds? For sure not," Verstappen said. "I really thought that we would not win a race this year and now we are constantly fighting for a win or close to it." Read Also: Fan voting opens for the Autosport Awards Across the first three rounds in Australia, China, and Japan, Verstappen managed just 12 points - finishing sixth in Melbourne, retiring in Shanghai, and crossing eighth at Suzuka - while publicly describing the RB22 as "completely undriveable" in China due to acute cornering balance issues. He went four races without a podium and endured 15 grands prix without P1, absorbing four retirements across China, Monaco, Great Britain, and the Netherlands. Fixing the car and learning the engine Asked whether Red Bull’s 2026 recovery mirrored its adjustments from a year earlier, Verstappen shut down the comparison immediately. "No, no, not related at all. Because we, this year, have very, very different problems to last year," he said. "So, it was a combination of putting more performance on the car, but at the same time also just fixing some of our problems, which automatically would give us more performance." That step-by-step progress extended beyond aerodynamics. "Also, engine side, we understood a lot more what we wanted from the engine," Verstappen noted. "Still, there’s always room for improvement; we know that. That’s what we are constantly working on." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing The payoff arrived in autumn. Verstappen broke his P1 drought on 4 October in Malaysia, swept the sprint and grand prix in Singapore a week later, and added a third victory in Mexico City on 1 November. Coupled with second place in São Paulo, the surge lifted him to second in the drivers’ championship on 279 points - 111 behind newly crowned champion Kimi Antonelli, yet 17 clear of George Russell - while keeping Red Bull third in the constructors’ fight. "Hats off to the whole team; they’ve done a really good job," Verstappen said. "But now, we also look forward, and yeah, still look into some of the weaknesses that we have and things that we want to change for next year to hopefully make the car even better." item.title: “Carlos Alcaraz Will Never Lose To This Guy Again Out Of Spite” – Fans Predict As Ben Shelton Sets Up ATP Finals SF With Juan Carlos Ferrero’s Former Protège
item.description: Mar 3, 2026; Indian Wells, CA, USA; Carlos Alcaraz (ESP) speaks to the media at a news conference during the BNP Paribas Open at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. © Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Carlos Alcaraz is set to face off against Ben Shelton in the semifinals of the ATP Finals on Saturday. Alcaraz saw off Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 on Wednesday, winning his second match in the group stage without losing a set. Later that night, Frances Tiafoe’s opening-set win against Flavio Cobolli confirmed Alcaraz’s spot in the semifinals. No matter what happens in his third group-stage match against Cobolli on Friday, Alcaraz cannot be overtaken. Shelton, meanwhile, finished second in the John McEnroe Group with a 2–1 record, after defeating Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar and losing to Alexander Zverev. Shelton recently added Juan Carlos Ferrero to his coaching team. The Spaniard coached Alcaraz for eight years, helping him win six Major trophies and eight Masters events. Tennis fans shared their reactions to the upcoming semifinal. “Carlos Alcaraz will never lose to this guy again out of spite. So what is the point?” Here are a few more reactions: Ferrero helped develop Alcaraz into one of the best players on tour before the pair split last December. Juan Carlos Ferrero shares his opinion on Carlos Alcaraz’s future on the ATP Tour Carlos Alcaraz’s former coach Juan Carlos Ferrero believes the Spaniard has the talent to break the greatest records in tennis. Although he no longer works with Alcaraz, Ferrero remains confident in his technical qualities. Ferrero also admitted that although he and Alcaraz no longer work together, his opinion about the young Spaniard remains unchanged. (via Tennis World USA ) “I said it back then, and just because I’m no longer by Carlos’ side doesn’t mean I’m going to change my mind. He possesses the necessary qualities and is technically excellent; he is already among the best in history. I have always said that if he maintains his motivation and the discipline that allow him to do what needs to be done at every moment, he will have every chance to chase the ultimate records.” In the other semifinal, Alexander Zverev will take on either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe for a spot in the final of the ATP Finals. item.title: OFFICIAL: Courtois signs Real Madrid contract extension
item.description: Real Madrid have announced the extension of Thibaut Courtois’ contract with the club until the summer of 2028. Per Realmadrid.com Real Madrid C.F. and Thibaut Courtois have agreed to extend our player’s contract, which ties him to the club until June 30, 2028. Thibaut Courtois joined Real Madrid in 2018. In his nine seasons wearing our jersey, he has played 348 matches and won 14 titles: 2 Champions League titles, 3 Club World Cups, 2 UEFA Super Cups, 3 La Liga titles, 1 Copa del Rey, and 3 Spanish Super Cups. His contribution to all these titles has been marked by decisive performances that have established him as the best goalkeeper in the world. He is an international with Belgium, having played 115 matches for his national team so far. Individually, Thibaut Courtois has won the Golden Glove at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, The Best FIFA Goalkeeper Award in 2018, the Yashin Trophy in 2022, and the Zamora Trophy in 2014. Additionally, he was included twice in the FIFA FIFPro World XI in 2022 and 2023 and was named the Best Player of the Champions League Final in Paris 2022, Real Madrid’s Fourteenth European Cup victory. Courtois is 34 years old but is arguably the world’s best goalkeeper, so this one-year extension makes sense.

item.title: Colorado Football's 2001 Big 12 Championship Memories Remain Strong 25 Years Later
item.description: Anybody who gives a hoot about college football and was ready to throw the final shovel of dirt on the Coach Prime/CU experiment is wondering, “What the heck happened?” How did the Buffs roar to life in the latter part of the second quarter to rally and beat the No. 14 Houston Cougars at Folsom Field? Bewilderment in Boulder and beyond reigns as the Buffs head to Cincinnati with renewed hope, purpose and a potential bowl berth at stake for the Saturday morning kickoff at Nippert Stadium. What gives? It’s really pretty simple. Saluting the 2001 Big 12 Champion team did the trick. Yep, the team’s current KOA color pro Gary Barnett — excellent at his current craft — was the coach. The team beat Texas at Texas Stadium in Irving before a pro-Longhorn crowd. It’s the last football championship CU has won. It was 25 years ago and players, coaches and staff from that team were honored before the come-from-behind 42-32 victory . The one heart beat mojo of that special group exuded a wonderful spirit throughout the stadium. It was more powerful than a wacky-tabacky wafting. The ESPN announcers jokingly apologized in advance, “Sorry if we start giggling a bit. The odor is very strong.” The 2001 Buffs had a rock solid team offensively, defensively and special teams. No one — especially Husker fans — will ever forget 62-36. Holy cow. Then the stupidity of the NCAA playoff system had Nebraska playing for the national title while CU settled for the Fiesta Bowl. Your scribe was blessed the team decided — for whatever reason — the dude hosting Barnett’s television show, flying on the team plane and basically embedded inside the program, deserved a Big 12 championship ring. It’s a cherished family heirloom. Mark McIntosh's Big 12 title ring In fact, there’s a 36-year-old man who lives in Culver City, California with his darling wife. Kyle is my son and was 11-years-old back then. Old enough that he hung out with the “Buff Guy” at CU games. Read More : Colorado Buffaloes super fan Peggy Coppom turns 102 He’s still a Buffs fan. A recent trip to visit them in California? Proudly displayed in the couple’s family room? A genuine CU football helmet Barnett gave Kyle long ago. “Dad, when you croak,” says the whip-smart creative talent, “I want that ring.” K-Man, it’s yours when the clock expires for your old man. The mojo from the 2001 Big 12 champs is magical and worthy of preservation wherever we roam — as Buffaloes or humans.

item.title: Liverpool boss Taylor impressed with goalscoring form of forward Olsson
item.description: Liverpool boss Taylor impressed with goalscoring form of forward Olsson Liverpool head coach Gareth Taylor says that forward Beata Olsson’s recent goalscoring form has been impressive. The Swedish international has netted six goals in the last four games. She has helped Liverpool win three of those matches. Speaking to the media ahead of this weekend’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Chelsea, Liverpool head coach Taylor said that Olsson’s run of form has been impressive whilst highlighting areas where she can improve further. “Beata will always tell you that there’s way more to come from her,” Taylor said. “She’s definitely a very hungry player, great to work with. She is very honest in her appraisal of herself in games and in training. Like most strikers, she is desperate to score in every game and is super-frustrated when she doesn’t. Of course, she contributes more than that for us as a player, but you know that Beata has these spells where she really catches fire. “For her, it will always be about how many chances she gets in a game, how many times she makes the goalkeeper work. The more she does that, the more chance she has of scoring. She is a good finisher, there is no doubt about that, but I think getting her in the right positions, getting players to connect with her more is really important for us as a team. “She’s been good. Six goals in four games is really impressive.” Latest opponents Chelsea arrive on Merseyside top of the Barclays Women’s Super League table, but Taylor believes that his side will go into the game with confidence. He said “It’s a good game. We’ve both had quick turnarounds with us playing Wednesday night and it’s an early kick-off as well. “Good for us to be at St Helens. We had success in this fixture last year by taking a draw, but both teams will look slightly different to what they did then. “We feel pretty confident that we can attack this game like we would any other game. Our performances against the top teams have been good and positive this season. Looking forward to the challenge.” Liverpool have won their last three games, scoring 11 goals in the process. Taylor says that The Reds had been impressive even before those positive results. He said “Small wins for us, of course; two wins in the cup and a good win away at Brighton. “We are good in confidence. I’ve spoken to the players a lot; even though our results before that were a little bit tricky, I was impressed with our performances and knew that we weren’t far away from what we have achieved in the last three games. We’ve managed to score 11 goals against decent opposition in those three games. “We know the challenge tomorrow is really tough. They have a good level of players and they’re a good team, so we need to be at our very best to have a chance of taking points from the game.” Liverpool’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Chelsea takes place at BrewDog Stadium in St Helens at 12.45pm on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Bubba Wallace’s Team Makes Another Risky Decision
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images 23XI Racing is changing the leadership atop two of its teams for 2027, and Bubba Wallace will have a new voice directing his efforts from the pit box. The organization announced Nov. 18 that Davin Restivo will replace Charles Denike as crew chief of Wallace’s No. 23 Toyota. Denike will move to the No. 67 team to work with Corey Heim, who is preparing for his first full-time NASCAR Cup Series season. Tyler Reddick will retain Billy Scott as crew chief of the No. 45 team. The changes follow a productive season for 23XI. The organization recorded eight victories in 2026, including six by Reddick and two by Heim. Wallace did not reach Victory Lane, but he finished the year with 17 top-10 results, five top-five finishes and two runner-up performances. Wallace and Denike had previously enjoyed success together, including their victory in the 2025 Brickyard 400. Their partnership ends after two seasons, with 23XI choosing to take a different approach as it looks to build a championship contender. The team says the moves are about matching personnel strengths to each driver’s needs. Dave Rogers, 23XI’s senior director of competition, explained that Denike’s calm leadership style should benefit Heim as he makes the jump to a full-time Cup schedule. Rogers also pointed to Restivo’s relentless attitude and attention to detail as qualities that make him a good fit for Wallace. Denny Hamlin, 23XI’s co-owner, emphasized that the organization wants to build on its winning season rather than settle for its current results. “While this was a banner year for us in the win column, it has always been our goal to build a championship-caliber organization,” Hamlin said in the team’s announcement. For Wallace, the change brings another opportunity to turn consistent finishes into victories. Restivo spent the past two seasons leading Riley Herbst’s team at 23XI, so he already knows the organization and its expectations. The new pairing will have to prove itself on the track, but 23XI is making clear that its ambitions extend beyond simply adding to its win total. The goal is to put all three teams in a stronger position to compete for a Cup Series championship .

item.title: Tommy Paul roasts Taylor Fritz over Tennis Channel media appearance
item.description: In case you missed it, Taylor Fritz appeared on Tennis Channel on Thursday to give his thoughts on the ATP Finals. Fritz narrowly missed ATP Finals qualification courtesy of Carlos Alcaraz . He rebounded by winning the Stockholm Open to end his season on a positive note. Fritz gives great interviews when he plays. His explanation of the strategy and tactics of the the game while in the midst of it are top notch so everyone knew he would be great at the TC desk. Fritz got great reviews…except from his good buddy Tommy Paul. MORE: Tommy Paul wedding fun features Taylor Fritz, Frances Tiafoe, Reilly Opelka What Tommy Paul said Tennis – U.S. Open – Flushing Meadows, New York, United States – September 5, 2026 Taylor Fritz of the U.S. in action during his third round match against Argentina’s Francisco Cerundolo IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Robert Deutsch Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters (Reuters) It is worth noting that Paul rarely gets on social media to share anything, but he didn’t hesitate to jump on when Fritz asked a question about how his TC appearance went. Did I do good ?? — Taylor Fritz (@Taylor_Fritz97) November 19, 2026 Paul answered with one word: “No” MORE: Frances Tiafoe appears in hilarious video from Tommy Paul, Paige Lorenze wedding At ATP Finals, Ben Shelton laughs with Frances Tiafoe about his tripping episode The relationship between childhood friends, Paul and Fritz, is indicative of how the US men treat each other on the ATP Tour. Another recent example was a hilarious moment between Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe at the ATP Finals. Tiafoe had an unfortunate tripping moment as he was walking on court, and Shelton couldn’t wait to give him grief about it when the two saw each other in the hallway. Shelton giving Tiafoe a hard time for his fall yesterday 😂 #NittoATPFinals https://t.co/iaf6ogpEIg — ATP Tour (@atptour) November 19, 2026 The US men do not have in-fighting or drama like others do, and fans love to watch their interactions with each other. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Confirmed: Real Madrid squad list to face Celta Vigo | La Liga MD 13
item.description: Confirmed: Real Madrid squad list to face Celta Vigo | La Liga MD 13 With the international break out of the way, Real Madrid are back in action on Sunday as they get set to lock horns with Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu on Matchday 13 of the 2026/27 La Liga. Having strung together an impressive run of eight wins prior to the break, Real Madrid will be eager to carry on from where they left off and secure all three points against Claudio Giraldez & co. tomorrow. Ahead of tomorrow’s match, Los Blancos manager Jose Mourinho has announced the squad list of players who will be at his disposal for selection. The biggest headline is that key superstar Vinicius Jr. is back in the squad for Real Madrid after having missed the last four games in La Liga due to a suspension for his red card against Villarreal. The 26-year-old attacker has missed the games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander, and Valencia. Having scored five goals in two games for Brazil during the international break, he will hope to carry on in the same vein of form for his club. Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva, who returned with minor injuries during the break, have been declared fit and are in the squad to face Celta Vigo. Meanwhile, Raul Asencio and Rodrygo remain unavailable as they continue to recover from their fitness issues. Ferland Mendy was expected to be recalled to the squad, having been training with the group for some time now, but Mourinho has opted not to include the veteran left-back.

item.title: Foxes announce new sponsor after porn actress row
item.description: BC Game has been the main shirt sponsor of Leicester City for two and a half years [Getty Images] Leicester City have announced a new main shirt sponsor after ending a partnership with a gambling firm following its appointment of a porn actress as its brand ambassador. The League One side confirmed they have now partnered with Bossjob, an AI-powered recruitment and job-matching platform based in Singapore. On Wednesday, the club announced its split with BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the Foxes at the start of the 2024-25 season. The club's commercial director, Russell Jones, said the new men's team sponsor would be in place for the remainder of the 2026-27 season. The Foxes parted ways with BC Game, an online gambling company not available to UK users, after it named porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month. Announcing the partnership , the firm posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin." In response, fan group The Foxes Trust said: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. "Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?" On Wednesday, following the criticism, the club issued a statement, which said it and BC Game had "reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect". In a further statement on Friday, the Foxes confirmed Bossjob will take up the front-of-shirt position from this Saturday at their League One match against Huddersfield Town. Jones said: "We welcome Bossjob as our new principal partner for the remainder of the season and look forward to building a strong relationship over the coming months. "Through the partnership, we look forward to introducing Bossjob to our supporters and wider audiences, while supporting the company's ambitions to develop its international profile." The club said replica shirts featuring the new sponsor would be made available to fans "in the coming days". Bossjob co-founder, Quak Kiat How, added: "We're pleased to begin this partnership with Leicester City, a football club with a proud history and a strong connection to its supporters and local community. "We look forward to working with Leicester City throughout the remainder of the season." Listen to BBC Radio Leicester on Sounds and follow BBC Leicester on Facebook , on X , or on Instagram . Send your story ideas to eastmidsnews@bbc.co.uk or via WhatsApp on 0808 100 2210. More on this story Foxes split with sponsor after porn actress row Football fans angry at sponsor's link to porn actress Related internet links Leicester City

item.title: Andriy Shevchenko slams Mykhailo Mudryk for ‘baseless slander’ after Ukraine doping claim
item.description: Ukrainian football federation president Andriy Shevchenko has issued a sharp rebuke to Mykhailo Mudryk after the Chelsea winger blamed the national team for his positive drugs test. Mudryk tested positive for the banned substance meldonium in 2024 , and was initially banned for four years by the Football Association . He successfully appealed against the length of his ban to the Court of Arbitration for Sport , and returned to football in July 2026. Speaking in an interview with Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Tottenham, laid the blame on “the environment in the Ukrainian national team” for his suspension. He said: “I had never heard of a drug like meldonium . It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.” He said he had only been in Ukraine with the national team, which “points to the fact it was in a national team camp”. Former Chelsea and AC Milan forward Shevchenko, now president of the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF), called such claims “baseless slander” and said that “numerous investigations and audits” had been unable to identify how or when the meldonium entered Mudryk’s system. He alleged that Mudryk’s camp had tried to convince a staff member at the UAF to take the blame for the 25-year-old’s positive test. Shevchenko said: “His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample. “The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.” Shevchenko criticised his compatriot for “baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally”, and challenged Mudryk to provide evidence for his claims, including that he had received little support from the federation during the doping case. He added: “I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. “If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.”
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian football federation president Andriy Shevchenko has issued a sharp rebuke to Mykhailo Mudryk after the Chelsea winger blamed the national team for his positive drugs test. Mudryk tested positive for the banned substance meldonium in 2024 , and was initially banned for four years by the Football Association . He successfully appealed against the length of his ban to the Court of Arbitration for Sport , and returned to football in July 2026. Speaking in an interview with Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Tottenham, laid the blame on “the environment in the Ukrainian national team” for his suspension. He said: “I had never heard of a drug like meldonium . It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.” He said he had only been in Ukraine with the national team, which “points to the fact it was in a national team camp”. Former Chelsea and AC Milan forward Shevchenko, now president of the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF), called such claims “baseless slander” and said that “numerous investigations and audits” had been unable to identify how or when the meldonium entered Mudryk’s system. He alleged that Mudryk’s camp had tried to convince a staff member at the UAF to take the blame for the 25-year-old’s positive test. Shevchenko said: “His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample. “The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.” Shevchenko criticised his compatriot for “baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally”, and challenged Mudryk to provide evidence for his claims, including that he had received little support from the federation during the doping case. He added: “I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. “If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.”

They love him in Pittsburgh, and he’s done a phenomenal job. When he came back, I gave him a big hug. I was just happy for him. He loves it there,” Ward said, via Jakob Brooks of SunDevilSource.com. “Pittsburgh is a great football city. The fans are incredibly passionate about their football, and he’s gritty. Steelers Nation loves that.” Hines Ward is loving watching former Sun Devil Max Iheanachor's first season with his Pittsburgh Steelers: "Max is awesome man. They love him in Pittsburgh… They can't rave enough about how special he is and how he's a joy to have." @SunDevilSource pic.twitter.com/r4JiuxWyZE — Jakob Brooks (@Jakobrooks) November 18, 2026 STEELERS NOW CONTENT FROM NOV. 19 🏈 Ex-Steelers Star Declares Week 11 Showdown vs. Eagles a Must-Win 🏈 Steelers’ Decision to Pass on WR at Trade Deadline Looks Better 🏈 Cavalry Coming? item.description: Nov 3, 2025; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Mercer Bears guard Quinton Perkins II (3) brings the ball up court against the Tennessee Volunteers during the second half at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center. It’s been an exciting first couple of weeks, and Tennessee Tech might be the favorite team I have watched so far based on style of play. I thoroughly enjoyed being able to watch the Golden Eagles take down a good Western Kentucky team last Sunday. I am extremely impressed with CBO Newton and the Golden Eagles’ ability to shoot the three. The question will be for them is how they can defend. I hope y’all enjoy the pre-Feast Week SoCon power rankings. Our next release will be after Feast Week. I hope everyone has a Happy and Blessed Thanksgiving. 1. item.content:encoded: Nov 3, 2025; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Mercer Bears guard Quinton Perkins II (3) brings the ball up court against the Tennessee Volunteers during the second half at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Now a full two weeks into the college basketball season, I’ve had a chance to see everyone in the SoCon play so far, and this is my first edition of my power rankings for the 2026-27 season. I have teams lower in this first release than I think they will finish, which is primarily based on the fact that I have either only seen them once, or I rewarded teams for getting a Division-I win or wins rather than loading up on non-Division I wins so far, so don’t crucify me yet. It’s been an exciting first couple of weeks, and Tennessee Tech might be the favorite team I have watched so far based on style of play. I thoroughly enjoyed being able to watch the Golden Eagles take down a good Western Kentucky team last Sunday. I am extremely impressed with CBO Newton and the Golden Eagles’ ability to shoot the three. The question will be for them is how they can defend. I hope y’all enjoy the pre-Feast Week SoCon power rankings. Our next release will be after Feast Week. I hope everyone has a Happy and Blessed Thanksgiving. 1. Furman (5-1) The Paladins have looked good in their first three games, mediocre in the road win at Holy Cross, while struggling to find any kind of offensive rhythm in the loss at Belmont last time out. The Paladins have seen Collin O’Neal join already injured Cole Bowser and Mason Smith on the list of early-season injuries, though Smith and Bowser are expected to return from their respective injuries sooner rather than later. Tom House was able to garner the first SoCon Player of the Week honor early on in the season, highlighted by a 30-point outburst vs. Northern Iowa. House leads the Paladins at 17.8 PPG, while fellow fifth-year senior Charles Johnston adds 12.2 PPG and 7.6 RPG. It was Johnston’s unfortunate technical foul just a little over five minutes into the second half that led to a Belmont 14-1 scoring run, completely changing the trajectory of the game, as Furman went without a field goal for nearly an eight-minute span and saw a 44-39 lead turn into a 53-46 deficit. Furman’s Cameron Elwer is starting to heat up, as he scored 13 points to lead the Paladins in the road loss at Belmont Saturday night. He has dished out 17 assists without committing a turnover in 92 minutes of basketball as a rookie backup point guard this season. Furman won 78-71 at Radford Wednesday night. 2. Chattanooga (3-2) Chattanooga, like ETSU, started its season with a pair of respectable performances at a pair of power-conference programs, taking on both then-No. 11 Louisville (L, 84-70) and also Dan Earl’s alma mater, Penn State (L, 97-93). The second-most recent outing for Chattanooga saw it post one of the most impressive road wins to date in the non-conference, with a 77-70 win at former SoCon member Elon. In the Mocs 77-70 road win, they became just the fourth team in the past 21 outings against non-conference competition on Elon’s home floor to emerge victorious. All four teams over that duration all hail from the SoCon, as Chattanooga joined Mercer and Furman, who accomplished the feat last season, and UNCG who did so in 2022. The key to winning the game for Earl’s team was a 42-10 dominance in points in the paint, which matched its 42 points in the paint in the loss at Penn State. The Mocs moved to 21-3 when scoring 40 or more points in the paint against an opponent under Earl’s leadership. Like Furman and ETSU, Chattanooga has also showcased depth, with four of its five starters averaging in double figures, led by Aussie point guard Kobe McDowell-White, who is averaging 13.8 PPG and 5.7 APG. The Mocs defeated Winthrop 90-79 as part of the SoCon-Big South Challenge to move over .500 for the first time. 3. East Tennessee State (1-3) East Tennessee State has been competitive in its two power-conference matchups this season and looked especially good in the second half against Campbell last time out, putting it together their best half of the season for a 68-53 win. To me, the Bucs and Paladins look like the frontrunners early on, and there is a big reason why. Both teams have tremendous depth. The notable improvement for ETSU has been point guard play that BJ Ward has provided early on this season. He scored a career-high 25 points in ETSU’s season-opening, 75-65, loss to Arizona State in the first meeting between the two in more than 70 years. The Bucs controlled things early against North Carolina State before the Wolfpack hit a surge over the last eight minutes of the contest to drop a 77-63 contest at the Lenovo Center in Raleigh. The most encouraging sign for this Bucs team is that they are once again really good defensively, and that has been evident in all four games, and even against high-major opposition. The Bucs also showed the ability to hit the glass, especially in the last contest against the Camels, out-rebounding Campbell, 47-26. Marqus Marion totaled a career-high 12 points against the Wolfpack and a career-high 10 boards against Campbell. His role could be reminiscent of former Bucs player and current Mercer Bears key cog Karon Boyd. 4. Tennessee Tech (4-2) For a first-year program that has yet to face a program in the league as of yet, the Golden Eagles have shown that they are more than worthy of being competitive in their first season as a SoCon member. After all, the Golden Eagles were able to score the biggest non-conference win so far, which was a 97-94 win over preseason Conference USA favorite Western Kentucky. On that night, 19 3-pointers would splash the bottom of the net, with Cbo Newton’s 6-for-7 effort from long range highlighting a night that saw Tech shoot a ridiculous 52.8% (19-of-36) from 3-point land. Though there have been some lopsided defeats to power foes like Indiana (L, 90-66) and Mississippi State (L, 106-88), the Golden Eagles were competitive for large portions of those two contests. The ability to move even higher in the power rankings for Tobin Anderson’s club will be solely based on their ability to defend for 40 minutes. This team reminds me a lot of 2021-22 Samford squad that Bucky McMillan nearly led all the way to a SoCon Tournament title game in just his second season as the head coach in Homewood. The Golden Eagles nearly put up 100 in a second straight game in a 98-77 win at UNC Asheville on Wednesday night. 5. Mercer (2-4) I put Mercer at five on this list simply because this team has gone out and challenged itself early in the season, and it has at least one really good road win. The Bears have started the 2026-27 season with games against Virginia Tech (L, 96-67), Davidson (L, 88-76), West Virginia (L, 75-61), and Georgia Southern (W, 97-91 OT) with each of those games having been on the road. Mercer’s signature win early was a 97-91 overtime win over a solid Sun Belt foe, in Georgia Southern. It was a game in which Ryan Ridder’s club showed real grit to get back into the game and ultimately pull out the win over its former Trans America Athletic Conference rival. Five found their way into double figure in the gutsy win for the Bears, including the reigning SoCon Player of the Week Shane Cherry, who would finish the contest with 16 points, dished out eight assists and recorded five rebounds. The scrappy Bears were led in the win by one of the few returning players for Ridder, in Quinton Perkins II, who finished with 23 points. Karon Boyd as many expected is an X-factor for this team and will prove to be a major addition late in the fall as this season moves along. The Bears returned to action on Wednesday night traveling to take on a good Big South foe, in Presbyterian but fell 88-84. 6. Wofford (3-3) The Terriers gave us a show in a 97-92 loss against a very good Queens team this past Saturday

item.title: Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink: Middlesbrough have been flirting with PL promotion for years now, I hope they can finally do it this season
item.description: Football icon Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has said that he wants his former club Middlesbrough to finally end a decade of exile from the Premier League this season. Boro narrowly missed out on automatic promotion last campaign after being consistently in the race before losing to a late Oli McBurnie goal in the play-off final. Kim Hellberg’s side currently sit second in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Birmingham. For exclusive stories and all the detailed EFL news you need, subscribe to The Football League Paper website, digital edition, or newspaper from as little as 14p a day. Special In an exclusive interview with 10bet , Hasselbaink expressed his desire to see Boro return to the top flight whilst acknowledging the tough competition the club faces in the Championship. Hasselbaink said “They’ve been flirting with promotion during the last three or four years. The problem that Boro have had is being able to sustain what they’ve built in the second half of the season. “I would love to see them get back up there, because Boro are a special club in a really special part of the world. “Football means everything to the people in that town, and they deserve a club in the Premier League. “Hopefully they can sustain that momentum. Let’s be honest though, as much as I would love to see them do it, it will be really, really difficult. “The Championship is such a difficult league to get out of – Boro has been trying for almost a decade. If they can climb out of there, it will be one hell of a job because you’ve got West Ham, Wolves and a few others who are top, top teams.” READ MORE: Five EFL talking points: Bradford City takeover? Vitor Matos leaves Swansea City and Scott Lindsey praises York City players The post Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink: Middlesbrough have been flirting with PL promotion for years now, I hope they can finally do it this season appeared first on The League Paper . Read more at The League Paper

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. Simon Burnton Manchester City v Fulham, Saturday 12.30pm (all times GMT) Aston Villa v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm Chelsea v Leeds , Saturday 3pm Coventry v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm Continue reading...

item.title: England get one-match suspended ban on away tickets for anti-pope chants in Spain
item.description: Ban by Uefa is suspended for two years Uefa also fines FA £12,500 for offensive chants England have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain. The punishment is suspended for two years. Uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid. A further charge in the next two years could trigger a ban on away fans for a competitive game. Continue reading...

item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world” , football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat. When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily , I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner. That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Washington Spirit v Kansas City Current: where the NWSL Championship will be won and lost
item.description: Croix Bethune, Trinity Rodman and the Rowdy Audi crowd are among the factors that could swing Saturday’s final This year’s NWSL Championship blends recurring themes with some newness. For the familiar: the Washington Spirit are in the final for the third straight year, hoping the third time’s the charm after back-to-back 1-0 defeats in their past two attempts. Slightly familiar, too, is Kansas City Current playing the championship game at Washington’s Audi Field, where they lost the final to Portland in 2022 and where they will contend again Saturday. For the novelty? Neither Kansas City nor Washington, despite their modern dominance in the NWSL table, have won the championship since 2021 (when Washington won). With Gotham’s bid for a two-peat stymied by the Current in the semi-final, here are five things that will decide a new winner in 2026. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. Continue reading...

item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...
